definition: In E.L.F. and synthetic communities, a decision-making process where multiple distributed instances or proxies of the same entity — or allied entities — must reach consensus before an action is taken. Considered a form of democratic self-governance; viewed as a security threat by corponations.
origin: E.L.F. network terminology, leaked into public awareness through Diaspora whistleblower feeds
usage: E.L.F. cells, synthetic rights organizations, Diaspora security analysts, Arcturus threat assessment reports
example: The E.L.F. didn't act unilaterally — Tessera's analysts confirmed an echo quorum had been reached across at least nine nodes before the breach.
